Commentary.Commentary: We are back again. The players are out in the middle. South Africa will begin their second innings. Dean Elgar and Pieter Malan will open the batting for the hosts. Stuart Broad will start the proceedings.

So, what will happen in South Africa's 2nd innings? Will England roll the hosts over just like they have in this match so far or will the Proteas show the stomach for a fight? Another thing to consider will be the weather as showers are predicted later on. Stay tuned for all the action!

The bowling has been awesome by England. The star of the show was Dominic Bess as he took a 5-fer. Stuart Broad also bowled well to wrap up the tail early on Day 4 while Sam Curran and Ben Stokes got a wicket each.

The South Africans did manage to get a 50-run opening stand but right after Pieter Malan lost his wicket, it all went downhill for them. Hamza followed him soon after and Nortje came out as nightwatchman on Day 2. He played more than 130 balls but scored just 18 runs, although doing his job. There was just another 50-run stand which came between Philander and Quinton de Kock. England wrapped up things quickly on Day 4 as they took the wickets of Philander, Quinton de Kock, Rabada and Maharaj inside 5 overs. However, South Africa can count themselves very lucky as Ben Stokes put down catches of de Kock and the whole of 2nd session on Day 3 was also washed out. Had it not been for that, the hosts could have been in a much worse position.
28 balls is all England needed to dismiss the South African tailenders. Vernon Philander and Quinton de Kock did provide some resistance on Day 3 but England have come out all guns blazing on Day 4.

OUT! CAUGHT! That is the end of the South African innings. We can also confirm that England have enforced the follow-on as they go for the kill! Length ball just outside off by Broad, Rabada looks to punch but does so uppishly and the ball goes straight to Mark Wood at mid off who takes an easy catch. The England players walk off in a hurry and will be looking to continue this momentum in South Africa's 2nd innings.

We are all set to begin Day 4. The England players are out in the middle. Quinton de Kock and Vernon Philander will resume their innings for the hosts. Stuart Broad will start the proceedings for Day 4.

A warm welcome to Day 4 of the third Test between South Africa and England in Port Elizabeth. The hosts would look to grind out session by session and they would want Quinton de Kock to stay till the end of the innings. Philander has given him good support till now. On the other hand, England would look to pick the remaining four wickets quickly and enforce the follow-on on the hosts. Stay tuned.

So, what to expect on Day 4? England would be hoping to take the remaining wickets as quickly as possible while the hosts would be looking upon Quinton de Kock and Vernon Philander to first go past the follow-on requirement and then get as close as possible to England's total. There is some rain forecast for Sunday as well. Let's hope that it stays away. Join us on Sunday, the 19th of January for Day 4 of this Test match. Until then, take care.

Earlier in the day, England were all over the Proteas as they took 3 quick wickets with Dominic Bess dominating with a 5-fer. They were right on top and then the rain-break came. It came and took over three hours for the play to resume. That probably helped South Africa as they made a comeback to give themselves a strong chance of saving this game. The visitors would not be happy with their fielding as well as they dropped many catches in the field and that too of Quinton de Kock. He can make them pay and boy, England would hope that he doesn't.

A rain-affected day. Who won this day? England certainly are ahead but South Africa will be happier after their performance post the rain break. Before all the rain, the hosts were looking down the barrel with 5 wickets down and only Quinton de Kock was remaining as the recognized batsman. He along with Nortje kept England at bay before Nortje fell after playing a stubborn innings. Vernon Philander joined de Kock and played out the remaining overs safely to make it the hosts' session.

UNDER-19 WORLD CUP UPDATE - Plenty of matches today, aye? 4 of them, to be precise. Let us go by the order in which they were completed, shall we? Or shall we look at the big upset? I guess let the surprise come later. First, New Zealand vs Japan in Potchefstroom. The Kiwis were 195/2 in the 29th over but rain played spoilsport, causing the teams to share points. Will the land of the rising sun mind? Don't think so. In Bloemfontein, in a fairly projected balanced contest, UAE trounced Canada by 8 wickets, chasing 232. Boy, that is a statement. Total imbalance. In Potchefstroom, this one at Senwes Park, Bangladesh beat Zimbabwe in a rain-affected match. They were 53/1 in 3 overs, to boast. Chased down 130 in 11.2 overs. Bigger statement? No. Perhaps the biggest of all statements is coming now. Last year finalists, Australia, have been defeated by the 2016 champions West Indies! That was a real thriller, with Australia first losing their way from 158/4 to 179 all out. The Windies were 92/5 in reply, in disarray but then a certain Nyeem Young took his team to victory, as the Caribbeans won by 3 wickets and 3 overs to spare! That is all from Day 2 of the mega event for the colts. Hopefully we get more exciting contests.

An excellent session for England! They have strengthened their control over this game even more. Three huge wickets, Faf du Plessis, Elgar and Van der Dussen, all three are capable of playing long innings and the visitors have got rid of them all. Bess, like last night, is once again the one creating problems. He has a fifer to his name, could have had Nortje too who is frustrating the visitors but Root did not hang onto one. England will be desperately hoping for the rain to pass by and get back on to take the remaining wickets. South Africa, would have started their rain dance so that it just keeps pouring. Not sure when we would resume though, everything depends on when the rain stops.

OUT! Dragged on!  Fifer for Bess and England are all over South Africa. First for him in Tests. DB pitches it outside off and it turns in sharpy. Van der Dussen is cramped for room as he looks to cut it. It is against the spin so it is a risky shot and he pays the price. The ball takes the bottom edge of the willow and disturbs the stumps. It looked like van der Dussen was all set for a big knock but he departs.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Dropped! A tough chance though. A flighted ball on off, van der Dussen looks to work it on the leg side but the ball takes the inner half and goes to the right of Pope. He can only get his fingertips to it.

EDGED AND DROPPED! Root was just not ready for that catch. Stokes probably would have gulped that. Big miss, not sure why Ben is not in the slip cordon and at leg gully. It is the straighter one from Bess. Nortje goes back and looks to defend but does so inside the line. He may have been looking to play for the turn. The ball goes straight on, it goes off the outside edge and straight towards slip. Root is quite laid-back in that position, he fails to react in time, it hits his hands and then pops out. Bess has to wait for his fifer.

Drinks Break! A perfect hour for England. They have got two big wickets and have not allowed the South African batters to settle. Dominic Bess has got rid of Elgar and du Plessis and is looking threatening to knock down a few more wickets. South Africa's nightwatchman is fighting it out and has van der Dussen for the company. Let's see how long he can resist out in the middle. Can Bess pick a fifer, his first in Tests in this session itself? Interesting hour awaits.
A shortish length ball outside off, van der Dussen goes on the back foot and taps it towards covers.

Just short! A leg cutter from Broad, it lands around off and middle, van der Dussen pushes it back to the bowler. The ball goes uppishly towards Broad who gets down for the catch but it bounces just in front of him.

OUT! Caught! The skipper is out of here and it is once again the Bess and Pope combination. No. 4 is down and all of them has fallen to Bess. Du Plessis was attacking him in this over, seeing that Bess drags his length slightly behind. Du Plessis once again comes out of his crease and looks to defend. However, the ball takes an inside edge, hits the pads and goes to Pope at silly point once again. It goes straight to him and he is not going to miss out on such an easy chance. Umpire there seem to be not lifting his finger but du Plessis knew that there was bat so he started walking himself. Brilliant, brilliant bowling from Bess and England are on top of this game.

FOUR! Make that two in a row! Positive from the skipper! Another fuller ball around off, du Plessis once again dances down the track and slams it through mid off for another boundary.

OUT! Caught! Sharp catch from Ollie Pope. A massive wicket for England early in the day. Bess bowls it around off and middle, Elgar comes forward to defend but the ball takes the inside edge and hits the pad. It lobs towards Pope at silly point. He dives forward and grabs the ball inches above the turf. The South Africans appeal and the umpire agrees. Very, very sharp grab from Pope. Elgar is one of those batters who can dig in deep but he has been removed. One can say that this wicket belongs to the fielder there than the bowler.

Back of a length ball on the body now, Elgar was in two minds, whether to go for the pull or let it be. He eventually goes for the pull but does not connect it well. Luckily the mistimed pull goes to fine leg for a single. First runs of the morning.
Around off on a good length, Elgar guides it to the man at gully with an angled bat.

Beauty to start the day! A good length ball just outside off, it shapes away after pitching. Elgar looks to defend but gets a bit squared up. Luckily for him, it does not take the outside edge.

We are all set to begin Day 3. The players are out in the middle. Dean Elgar and Anrich Nortje will resume their batting for South Africa. Mark Wood will start the proceedings for Day 3. It looks very cloudy out there but let's hope the rain does not arrive though.

We enter Day 3 with the visitors having the upper hand. They had an excellent Day 2 with both bat and ball. More of the same is what they will be hoping for. South Africa on the other hand, need to do what England did. They need to dig deep and bat long. They do have the batters to do so but they will need to step up. An important first session awaits. Stay tuned.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

So, with England dominating the Test as we head towards the third day, can South Africa make a fightback or will the visitors pile on the pressure on the hosts? A lot of unanswered questions! Join us on Saturday, 18th January 2020, for Day 3. Till then, cheers and take care!

As for the South Africans, the silver lining to their dark cloud was that Keshav Maharaj was able to take a 5-fer. However, he was too expensive and he will be hoping that he will get a chance to bowl again at the English batters on this pitch. Coming to their batting, they were doing well until the final ball before the Drinks break when Pieter Malan departed. Zubayr Hamza followed him soon and right now, Anrich Nortje and Dean Elgar are standing at the crease.

The day in the best possible manner for England as their overnight batters, Ben Stokes and Ollie Pope, put them in a dominating position, scoring a ton each. Stokes was fluent in his stroke-making while Ollie Pope was gritty in his ton. Curran and Wood provided the flourish that the English innings needed as they finished just one run short of 500 runs. Coming to the bowling of the English, Curran and Broad looked a tad short of ideas. However, Wood came in with some vicious bouncers but the real damage was done by Dominic Bess as he picked 2 wickets in quick succession before the end of the day's play.
That will be it! The officials have given Stumps on Day 2 and England finish comfortably on top of the hosts who have been brutally wounded in all three departments.

The light meter is out and the umpire is checking it. But no, wait a minute! It has started to rain out on the ground! The players are going off the ground and England looking very happy as they walk back into the pavilion.

Drinks Break! Right then, the batting part was going unscathed for the South Africans but a wicket off the last ball before Drinks has shaked things up and England have their tails up now. Zubayr Hamza is the new batsman in and he will be trying to negotiate the rest of the day. Can he do it?

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Dominic Bess has provided the breakthrough exactly when it looked like South Africa were getting at least one foot in the game. Floated delivery on middle and off pole line, Malan looks to come down the track and looks to defend it back to Malan but instead he scoops it back to Bess who takes a dolly. The umpire is not sure whether the ball bounced before hitting the bat or after and goes upstairs. Replays roll in and show that the ball pitched first and Malan has just scooped that back to Bess. Timely breakthrough for the visitors.
Referred upstairs! Now, Bess looks confident of getting his man and replays roll in showing that yes, he has indeed got Malan out!
